sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Rohan Verma, learned counsel for the applicant.
 Ms. Neelu Khetra, learned Dy.Govt.Advocate for the r  ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second bail application filed under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail to the applicant,
in connection with FIR/Crime No.187/2024, Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S.-Bhikangaon,
District-Khargone (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376,
376(2)(n), 344 of IPC, under Section 3/4, 5(L)/6, 5j(ii) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The first application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew his prayer after examination of the prosecutrix and her parents before the trial Court vide order dated 17.8.2024 passed in M.Cr.C.No.35177/2024.
2.
Prosecution story, in brief, is that at the time of incident the prosecutrix was minor around 17 years, but below 18 years.
On 23.3.2024 the prosecutrix left her house and went to Maharashtra alongwith the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31734 2 MCRC-45950-2024 applicant.
Both of them lived together around more than two months.
Meanwhile, he committed rape upon her several times.
Due to aforesaid act the prosecutrix got pregnant.
She was recovered on 11.6.2024 by the Police.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is submitted that at the time of incident prosecutrix was major lady, but her actual date of birth was not mentioned in the scholar register.

and father (PW-2) have been examined before the trial Court, but they have completely turned hostile and not supported the case of prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 11.6.2024.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for rejection of the bail application.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant - Vijay shall be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance on all such dates as may be fixed in this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:31734 3 MCRC-45950-2024 behalf by the trial Court during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of B.N.S.S.
8.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
9. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed off.
Certified copy, as per Rules.
